page.text:
Differentiation studies the first-order linear behavior of a function.
The derivative at a point is not merely a symbolic quotient: it is the
coefficient of the best linear approximation, with an error that is
negligible relative to the increment. This viewpoint explains the chain
rule, the mean value theorem, and the role of derivatives in local
approximation.
